playbook.intent: A week of merged pull requests and open RFCs has piled up, and the architect suspects coupling is creeping across service boundaries faster than anyone is writing it down. The forty-five minutes end with at most two topics argued through to a written outcome, each landing as an ADR or an RFC update shared with the wider engineering group rather than dissolving into meeting chat.
playbook.scope: Architect + 2-3 senior engineers walk the week's significant PRs + open RFCs. Goal: spot drift early (cross-service coupling, layering violations, missed reuse), promote good patterns to team patterns.md, queue ADRs.

success-criteria.criterion: The agenda carried no more than two topics and the pre-read for each went out a full day before the room met
Every topic discussed has a recorded outcome plus the tradeoffs that produced it, captured while the participants were still together rather than reconstructed afterwards
Each outcome lives in an ADR or an updated RFC in the repository, and the share log shows it reached engineering beyond the three people in the room
Patterns judged worth repeating were added to the team patterns file, and any implementation the review triggered has a kickoff on the calendar

stage.name: Triage Topics

tasks.task: Collect RFCs, ADRs, and tech-debt items needing decision
Cut to ≤2 topics for the 45-minute slot

stage.decision-gate: Advance only when the agenda is locked and pre-read is delivered.

stage.name: Run the Review

tasks.task: Each topic gets a presenter and a written proposal
Discuss tradeoffs; reach a decision or schedule follow-up
Capture the decision and the rationale on the spot

stage.decision-gate: Advance when every topic has a written outcome.

stage.name: Publish Decisions
stage.intent: Decisions belong in ADRs, not chat.

tasks.task: Convert every decision into an ADR or RFC update

stage.decision-gate: Required output: every decision lives in an ADR or RFC.
